text:
marta: Heads-up — ran a short bake on Llama2-13b + AWQ-int8 and saw intermittent perplexity spikes correlated with tail latency blips. suspecting kv-prefetch <-> continuous-batcher handoff jitter.

alex: can you share the run config and the waveform of the latency?

marta: config pasted below. spikes happen when a prefetched prefix enters a new microbatch slot. looks like cache TTL/slot align mismatch.

```
batcher:
  max_delay_ms: 6
  slot_align: false
  microbatch_size: 8
cache:
  ttl_ms: 150
  prefetch: true
quant_profile: awq-int8-v2
model: llama2-13b-seq2048
workload: chat-streaming, mean prompt len 120 tokens
```

ben: interesting. so if slot_align=false the batcher will cut across cached-prefetch boundaries? that could evict KV windows or create extra KV restores per step.

marta: exactly. we instrumented KV restore counts. baseline (slot_align=true) avg restores/token=0.002; with slot_align=false it jumps to 0.03 at peaks. perplexity +1.8 at peak buckets.

sarah: did you try changing ttl or microbatch_size? any tradeoff with latency?

marta: quick matrix:
- ttl_ms 150, microbatch 8, slot_align=false -> p90 latency 82ms, p99 420ms, perplexity delta +1.8
- ttl_ms 150, microbatch 8, slot_align=true  -> p90 78ms, p99 210ms, perplexity delta +0.2
- ttl_ms 300, microbatch 4, slot_align=false -> p90 88ms, p99 260ms, perplexity delta +0.5

alex: wow p99 drops a lot with slot_align true. seems aligning batch boundaries to cached prefix boundaries avoids extra KV chatter.

marta: also noticed AWQ-int8 kernel has slightly higher variance in kv-deserialization time vs fp8 runs, which amplifies jitter when handoffs are frequent.

ben: can you try adaptive-ttl (increase TTL for prefixes that see ongoing streaming) + keep slot_align=false to test whether longer TTL smooths it without strict alignment?

marta: on it. quick test: adaptive-ttl reduced restore spikes by ~60% but p99 still ~270ms; perplexity delta ~+0.4. still worse than slot_align=true.

sarah: for deploy profiles, we need to recommend: AWQ-int8 -> prefer slot_align=true for streaming low-latency SLAs, or use adaptive-ttl + smaller microbatch for non-aligned setups. document that in the model onboarding checklist.

alex: agree. also add a note that some quant backends (awq-int8 vs gptq) differ in kv-serialize latency — include a quick microbench in onboarding.

marta: leaving the experiment logs here. one weird artifact: when we force a cache miss at exact microbatch boundary, we sometimes get a short burst of 10-15ms extra CPU that cascades into batcher timers — probably contention in kvcache threadpool. I've filed a perf issue.

ci-bot: deploys/logs: run/2175302468-1 finished. artifacts: s3://redwood-ml/experiments/2175302468/metrics.csv

ben: next action items — (1) marta: run 24h sweep with slot_align=true vs adaptive-ttl for AWQ-int8 and GPTQ-int8; (2) alex: add microbench to onboarding template for kv-serialize/deserialize p50/p95; (3) sarah: update model onboarding doc recommending default batcher.slot_align=true for streaming profiles using AWQ-int8.

marta: acked. I'll include the raw metrics and a short note on when to prefer adaptive-ttl vs alignment (cost/latency/accuracy tradeoffs).

alex: thanks — this explains the weird production blips we saw last week on a dedicated pool.

marta: adding final note: FP8 runs didn't show the same restore jitter (lower KV deserialize variance), so FP8 remains a good candidate where model accuracy allows it. AWQ-int8 needs operational knobs.

sarah: perfect. will add to the onboarding checklist and share with infra and ops. :white_check_mark:
